en: The national flower Sampaguita releases its strongest fragrance at night to attract pollinating moths.
The Philippine eagle requires large, old-growth forests to hunt monkeys and build its massive nests.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, farmers decorate homes with colorful kiping made from pounded rice.
Ifugao farmers build stone-walled rice terraces that perfectly follow the natural contours of the mountains.
The national tree Narra drops its clusters of small yellow flowers during the dry season.
National Scientist Angel Alcala established coral reef sanctuaries in Apo Island to restore fish populations.
The national animal carabao cools its body by wallowing in mud because it lacks sweat glands.
Taal Volcano features a main crater lake situated on Volcano Island inside a larger caldera.
Mangyan weavers in Mindoro extract strong natural fibers from the buri palm to weave durable mats.
The rare Vanda sanderiana orchid grows high on tree branches in the damp forests of Mount Apo.
Hero Jose Rizal planted various fruit trees and crops in Dapitan to study local plant species.
The Banaue Rice Terraces use an ancient irrigation system to channel rainwater from mountain forest peaks.
